policy_title: Restore trust in police and end disproportionate policing tactics
stated: Restore trust and confidence in the police by acknowledging institutional racism, misogyny, homophobia, and disablism. End the routine use of stop and search and facial recognition software, and implement ongoing fitness-to-practice assessments on diversity for all officers.

source.quote: We believe in policing by consent, but this can only work if the police can rebuild trust with the communities they serve. Police Services need to acknowledge the institutional racism, misogyny, homophobia and disablism that have dominated policing for so long. Elected Greens will push for: • An end to the routine use of stop and search and to the use of facial recognition software. • Police Services to deliver ongoing fitness to practice assessments on diversity for all police officers and relevant civilian staff.

bearing_set.reason: Ending routine stop and search is a direct policing-tactic change with contested but non-negligible effects on crime rates and community safety outcomes.

Explicitly targets equal treatment by addressing institutional racism, misogyny, homophobia and disablism in policing; ending facial recognition bears directly on privacy rights — both core O9 indicators.

Ending routine stop and search reduces coercive, suspicion-free state interference with individuals, and ending routine facial recognition curtails mass surveillance — both directly improve the privacy and freedom-from-state-coercion indicators of personal liberty.

membership_note: Three clean bearings: O9 (equal-treatment/anti-discrimination by design), O10 (liberty/privacy gain from rolling back stop-and-search and facial recognition), and O5 (safety tradeoff — the concrete mechanism is reduced detection capacity, which may move crime-rate indicators upward, a non-negligible harm-side bearing). O15 (social trust) is a plausible secondary effect of restoring police legitimacy in minority communities but the primary mechanism routes through O9; not enough for a separate non-negligible verdict.
